scenes.title: Skill by skill: your work
scenes.sub: Ideation · scripting · AI prompting · editing · brand · business · imagination
scenes.say: Chapter eight. What the evidence says about each skill in your work.
A recall from chapter seven. Is YouTube packaging a kind or a wicked learning environment, and what does that mean for practice?
scenes.sayA: Semi-wicked. Feedback is noisy and delayed, so gut feel is unreliable. Use high volume, prediction logs and tests.
scenes.a: Semi-wicked: noisy, delayed feedback. Volume, prediction logs, tests.

scenes.head: Ideation: quantity breeds quality
scenes.bigl: number of ideas vs judged creativity
scenes.text: Hit rates stay roughly constant per attempt, so *more genuine attempts produce more hits*: Simonton's ~equal-odds rule~.
scenes.say: Ideation first. Hit rates stay roughly constant per attempt, so more genuine attempts produce more hits. This is Simonton's equal odds rule. In one study, the number of responses correlated 0.73 with judged creativity.

scenes.head: Generate alone, then pool
scenes.say: Generate alone first. Groups brainstorming together produce fewer ideas than the same people working separately and then pooling. A hybrid process, alone first and then together, produced more and better ideas, and was better at telling them apart.

scenes.text: Creators predicted the success of *other people's* acts better than managers did, but ~not their own~.
scenes.note: Prone to success fantasies? Outsource selection to peers and data.
scenes.say: Do not trust your own excitement about an idea. Among 339 circus professionals, creators predicted the success of other people's new acts better than managers did, but not their own. That is a direct warning for anyone prone to success fantasies. Outsource selection to peers and to data.

scenes.head: AI and ideas

items: Writers with AI ideas wrote better stories
Creativity training works: about half a standard deviation
Fix: ask the model to reason step by step

scenes.say: AI raises the floor but narrows the range. Writers given AI story ideas wrote better individually, but their stories became more alike collectively. Asking the model to reason step by step restored much of the diversity. And creativity can be trained: across 332 effect sizes, the effect was about half a standard deviation, with training in selecting and evaluating beating brainstorming training. Moderate constraints help. Too many or too few hurt.

scenes.head: Scripting: how writing skill develops
items: Knowledge-telling: write down what you know
Knowledge-transforming: shape it for a purpose
Knowledge-crafting: hold the reader's moment-by-moment experience
Pros write a few hours a day, every day. Binges breed block.
scenes.say: Scripting. Writing expertise develops in stages, from knowledge telling, writing down what you know, through knowledge transforming, to knowledge crafting, where you hold the reader's moment-by-moment experience in mind. Professionals compose for just a few hours a day, on a highly consistent schedule, because binge writing breeds writer's block.

scenes.head: What improves writing (effect sizes)
scenes.say: Instruction research favours explicit strategy instruction, at 0.82, help from peers, at 0.75, and specific goals for the finished product, at 0.70. Studying models helps, and watching real readers react to your own draft produced especially large gains.

scenes.head: Franklin's drill (worked example)
items: Pick a top intro. Reduce it to short hints.
Rewrite the intro from the hints, without looking.
Compare with the original. Note every gap.
scenes.say: Benjamin Franklin's method still works as a drill. He reduced essays to short hints, waited days, rewrote them from the hints without looking, then compared his version with the original. For you: pick a top intro, reduce it to hints, wait two or three days, rewrite it, and compare. That one exercise combines spacing, retrieval, generation and feedback.

scenes.head: Hooks
scenes.text: Curiosity arises ‘when attention becomes focused on a *gap in one's knowledge*’.
scenes.note: Check it: YouTube's intro metric, who's still watching at 30 seconds
scenes.say: Hooks rest on solid theory: curiosity arises when attention becomes focused on a gap in one's knowledge. Specific retention rules, like MrBeast's leaked memo obsessing over the first minute, are practitioner heuristics. But YouTube's own intro metric, the share still watching at 30 seconds, gives you an objective check.

scenes.head: AI prompting: the jagged frontier (758 consultants)
scenes.say: AI prompting. Official guidance agrees on the basics: be explicit, explain why, give three to five examples, and define success criteria with ways to test against them before tuning a prompt. Field evidence shows prompting skill rests on domain skill. On tasks within AI's abilities, 758 consultants produced over 40 percent higher quality, and were 25 percent faster. But on a task deliberately beyond those abilities, AI users were 19 points less likely to get it right.

scenes.head: Who gains from AI

items: More trust in AI, less critical thinking

scenes.say: The gains are real. ChatGPT cut professional writing time by 40 percent and raised quality by 18. Novice support agents gained 34 percent. But the losses are real too. Among 640 Kenyan entrepreneurs with an AI business mentor, high performers gained about 15 percent, while low performers did 8 percent worse, partly because they asked it harder questions.

scenes.head: The rule for AI
scenes.text: Learning? *Attempt first*, then use AI to critique and explain. Producing output? ~Only delegate what you could judge yourself~.
scenes.say: The rule that follows: when the goal is learning, attempt first, then use AI to critique and explain. When the goal is output, only delegate what you could judge yourself.

scenes.head: Creative editing
items: Good cuts manage attention: viewers missed about a quarter of cuts
Shot lengths vary in waves, like attention. Avoid uniform jump-cuts.
Taste: study 3 editors side by side; mixing styles teaches them better
Murch: emotion, then story, then rhythm (practitioner)
scenes.say: Creative editing. Good continuity editing manages viewer attention. Viewers asked to spot edits missed about a quarter of cuts, and a third when the cut matched sudden motion. Hollywood shot lengths have converged toward a rhythm that resembles human attention, so pacing should vary in waves, not run at a uniform jump-cut cadence. Taste is partly learning to tell styles apart, and mixing examples of different styles taught them better than one at a time. So study three editors side by side. Walter Murch's Rule of Six ranks emotion first, then story, then rhythm. And Ira Glass's taste gap closes only with a volume of work.

scenes.head: Brand building
items: Mental availability: easy to notice and recall
Distinctive assets: consistent colours, phrases, motifs
Brand vs activation ≈ 60:40 (B2B ≈ 46:54), disputed by Sharp
Trust, similarity and connection drive action
scenes.say: Brand building. Marketing science says brands grow mainly by reaching more buyers and being easy to notice, recall and buy. Distinctive assets, like consistent colours, phrases and visual motifs, need both fame and uniqueness. On the effort split, an analysis of 996 ad cases suggests about 60 to 40 between long-term brand building and short-term activation, or 46 to 54 for selling to businesses, though Byron Sharp calls that ratio very misleading. For a personal brand, repeated exposure increases liking, similarity drives attraction, and trust and connection best predict whether audiences act. Treat all of these as hypotheses to test.

scenes.head: Business
scenes.text: Founders taught to *state hypotheses and run rigorous tests* earned more revenue. Generic business training: ~relatively modest~ effects.
scenes.note: Keep a written experiment log, not a course collection
scenes.say: Business. In a randomised trial with Italian startups, founders taught to state theories, form hypotheses and run rigorous tests earned more revenue and pivoted more. Generic business training shows relatively modest effects. So keep a written experiment log rather than collecting courses, and use human mentors for hard strategic calls.

scenes.head: Imagination: an asset inside a container
scenes.bigl: of top physicists' and writers' key ideas came while thinking of something else
scenes.text: Your imagination is *not the enemy*. But incubation only helped on ~problems people had already worked on~.
scenes.say: Finally, imagination. Your imagination is not the enemy. About 20 percent of the most important ideas of 45 physicists and 53 professional writers arrived while they were thinking about something else. But incubation has conditions. In a 12-minute incubation study, only the group doing an undemanding task improved, and only on problems they had already worked on. Across 117 studies, incubation effects were modest, and grew with longer preparation. And vividness is not originality: immersive daydreaming was linked to lower originality.

scenes.head: Incubation vs escapism: five features
items: A loaded problem first: you've already worked on it
A bounded, low-demand activity: a walk, not hours in bed
Return to the work the same day
Imagine the process and obstacles, not the life after success
scenes.say: So the line between incubation and escapism has five features. A loaded problem first: something you have already worked on. A bounded, low-demand activity: a walk, not hours in bed. Capture, by voice memo or notebook. A return to the work the same day. And content about the process and the obstacles, not idealised outcomes. Students who imagined the process of studying studied more and scored higher. So imagine the cold open of your next video, or the obstacle you will hit in the edit, not the life after success.

scenes.text: No study has tested whether channelling MD into creative work *reduces* it. So ~cap it, write it, and track it~.
scenes.say: One caution. No study has tested whether channelling MD into creative work reduces MD. The risk is that an ideation slot becomes a sanctioned gateway into immersion. So cap it, write rather than just imagine, and track whether your total fantasy time goes down.
What is the rule for using AI when your goal is learning?
scenes.sayA: Attempt first, then use AI to critique and explain. Hints, not answers.
scenes.a: Attempt first, then AI critiques and explains

scenes.say: Name three of the five features that separate incubation from escapism.
scenes.sayA: A loaded problem first, a bounded low-demand activity, capture, a return to the work the same day, and imagining process and obstacles instead of success.
scenes.a: Loaded problem · bounded activity · capture · return · process, not success
